SMTO-EXE-0041 — The result of a data step was too large to return

GUID: fa1c068a-49a9-4378-8b15-e48ee44ef1fc
Slug: transform-output-limit
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO's data calculation finished, but its answer was bigger than about 1 MB, so SMTO couldn't take it back. Nothing was cut off or changed, and earlier results are still saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to return only what you need, such as a summary, totals, or fewer columns. A shorter answer fits within the size SMTO can take back from this kind of step.
  2. If you need every row, ask SMTO to split the work into smaller parts or to save the full result to a file. Smaller parts or a file keep all of the data without hitting the size limit.
  3. Check that the final answer covers everything you asked for. SMTO doesn't cut results short on purpose, so a missing part means a step is still needed.

What success looks like

  • The step completes and shows the full answer, or a file with the complete result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete earlier results or trim your data just to make the answer fit.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • With operation limits enforced, the python.transform worker's complete UTF-8 output exceeded 1,048,576 bytes and was rejected rather than truncated.

What this means

  • With transform limits enabled, the worker serialized the complete JSON output envelope and found its UTF-8 bytes exceeded 1,048,576. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • With transform limits enabled, the worker serialized the complete JSON output envelope and found its UTF-8 bytes exceeded 1,048,576.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the serialized output size and whether partitioning preserves the full intended result.

How to fix it

  • Reduce the transform output (fewer fields, aggregation, pagination) or split it into several transforms, or write the full result through a file-producing capability (agent_runtime.execution.transform_worker.main enforces the 1 MiB output limit). Do not silently truncate the result or remove required inputs.
  • Reduce or split the transformation output, or persist full results through a supported file-producing capability. Do not silently truncate the result.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • All required data is returned through valid smaller transformations or a supported file-producing capability without silent truncation.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
